how: One source mutation applied to the working tree, the named suite run against it, then the file restored before the next row. Convention (X14's, unchanged): `before` is the shipped source the row was run against and `after` is the text that replaced it, so `before` is always findable verbatim in `file` at the commit the table describes - including the rows whose fix landed after the test, where `before` is simply the pre-fix source and `after` the shipped code. An audit probe (does `before` occur in `file`?) was run over every row of this file and X14's at fix round 2; the two rows that had drifted with the source are re-recorded below against today's text, each re-run to red. Not a gate: this table quotes source, so a guard here would redden whenever that source legitimately moves. Run on maintainer-mac-1, 2026-10-31, lease X15-58alc.
